NORML Announces Free Fax to Congress
Opposing Congressional Override of DC Medical Use Initiative

October 2, 1999

Free Fax to Congress Opposing Congressional Override of DC Medical Use Initiative

Everyone should be contacting their U.S. Representative and two U.S. Senators now to register their opposition to the possible Congressional override of the DC medical use initiative.

The votes from the November, 1998 initiative (69% approval) were only recently counted and released, because of a prior attempt by Congress to block the initiative. It required the intervention of a federal court to order the results released.

See
Republicans Hold DC Hostage To Block Medical Marijuana,
After Clinton Vetos DC Appropriations Bill, Thereby Upholding Initiative 59.
Prohibitionism Uber Alles

Under terms of the law under which Congress granted limited "home rule" to the District, Congress now has 30 (working) days to override the new medical use law, or it becomes effective. This override provision applies regardless of whether a new law is adopted by the city council or by voter initiative. It has only been used a few times, and never to override a voter initiative.

Efforts are already underway by Rep. Bob Barr (R-GA) and others to move an override resolution forward.

Those wishing to weigh in with your members of Congress to urge them not to override the DC medical use initiative, can do so for free from the NORML web site (http://www.norml.org).

Simply go to the home page and click on "Fax Congress Now" in the upper left corner of the page. That will take you to a page where you can enter your name and address, and the software program will identify your members in Congress. Then you can elect from several letters, one of which focuses on this issue.

The letter can be edited, if you wish, before being faxed.

Please take this opportunity to let your members of Congress know how you feel, and pass this notice on to others.

Keith Stroup, Esq.

Executive Director, NORML
